purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and process program for the authoritative ruined fuel depot asset, preserving a legible bulk-fuel receiving, storage, transfer, dispensing and safety-containment system with believable vehicle access, operator control, maintenance circulation, terrain seating and coherent damage behavior.
ground_program: controlled service-road approach with gate or inspection point, tanker access, staff access and turning geometry appropriate to a bulk-fuel facility rather than a generic paved yard
fuel receiving area includes tanker unloading positions, hose or hard-pipe connections, spill-control surfaces and a credible route into the bulk-storage system
bulk-storage zone contains separated tanks or tank groups with visible transfer piping, valves, vents, foundations and secondary containment such as bunds, berms or curbed basins
pump and manifold area provides a legible transition between receiving, storage and dispensing or export lines without decorative dead-end pipework
dispensing or loadout area supports service vehicles, generators or distribution tankers with protected islands, hose points and vehicle clearances that do not conflict with bulk-storage containment
operator office or control room overlooks the receiving and transfer functions and contains alarm, shutdown, records and communications functions appropriate to hazardous-fuel handling
electrical, backup-power and control equipment are physically separated from the most hazardous transfer and storage zones while retaining believable cable and conduit routes
fire-protection provisions include hydrant, foam, water, extinguisher or emergency-isolation features positioned to protect tank, pump and transfer hazards
maintenance workshop, spares, spill-response equipment and service staging provide credible access to pumps, valves, tanks, vents, meters and transfer systems
drainage, grading, retaining features, tank foundations, containment berms and road elevations seat the depot into terrain without floating tanks, unsupported pipes or a single monolithic slab
upper_program: tank roofs, elevated valves, vents and inspection points use supported stairs, platforms, ladders and guardrails appropriate to equipment access rather than general occupied floors
any elevated pipe racks or transfer bridges are structurally supported at credible intervals and connect actual process endpoints
occupied control or administrative upper levels, if present, use enclosed supported stairs with usable landings and direct egress
roof zones preserve drainage, equipment access and separation from ignition-sensitive transfer areas
circulation: tanker traffic forms a believable entry, unloading and exit loop with adequate turning space and without crossing principal staff circulation where avoidable
staff circulation connects gate, operator control, storage observation, pump manifold, dispensing and maintenance areas while respecting containment barriers
maintenance circulation reaches tank bases, valves, pumps, pipe racks, electrical equipment, fire-protection systems and inspection platforms without requiring passage through active tanker lanes
emergency access remains possible to tank groups, pump areas and transfer zones from more than one direction where site geometry permits
equipment-only ladders do not substitute for architectural stairs in occupied spaces
damage_constraints: the ruined derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a fuel depot through surviving tank, containment, pump, manifold, transfer, control and vehicle-service relationships
favor localized tank fire, overpressure damage, pipe rupture, pump-house fire, spill staining, berm breach, corrosion, vehicle impact and vegetation intrusion over uniform random deletion
major tank or pipe failures must produce gravity-consistent debris, displaced panels, fallen pipe sections, scorched containment surfaces and localized spill evidence around the failed system
damage to tanks, racks, platforms, walls or roofs must resolve attached pipes, valves, ladders, railings, signs and fixtures so floating remnants are not left behind
preserve at least one legible exploration route from site entry through control, storage and transfer or dispensing functions
damage may disable individual tanks or transfer lines but must not erase the receiving-to-storage-to-transfer story or reduce the site to generic industrial clutter
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master
